summary: A settings panel for how much an agent may do on its own: an autonomy scale, on/off switches, a spend cap per run and free-text instructions. Any change brings up an "Unsaved changes" bar with Save and Reset, so people can review before the agent's behaviour changes.
use: When people need to decide whether the agent asks first or works alone.
When you want to cap what one agent run may spend.
When standing instructions for the agent should live next to its other settings.
When several settings changes should be reviewed and saved together.
features: An autonomy scale built from `levels` (Ask, Balanced and Autopilot by default), with the picked level's description shown under the heading.
One switch per entry in `toggles`, each with a label and an optional detail line.
A spend cap stepped up and down through the amounts in `caps`, shown with `formatCap`.
An instructions text box that is part of the same value.

A save bar that appears whenever the value differs from the last saved one. Save calls `onSave`, and if it returns a promise the button spins until it settles; Reset goes back to the last saved settings and calls `onReset`.
Works controlled through `value` and `onValueChange`, or holds its own state with `defaultValue`.
a11y: The autonomy scale is a role="radiogroup" labelled "Autonomy", and each step is role="radio" with aria-checked.
Each toggle is role="switch" with aria-checked and its label as aria-label.
The cap buttons are labelled "Lower cap" and "Raise cap", and the text box is labelled "Instructions".
The save bar is inert and aria-hidden while there is nothing to save.

faq.a: If the promise returned by `onSave` rejects, the button goes back to Save and the save bar stays up, because the settings still differ from the last saved ones.

faq.q: Can I change the autonomy levels?
faq.a: Yes. Pass `levels` with a label and description for each step. The scale lays out as many steps as you give it, and `autonomy` in the value is the index of the picked one.

faq.q: How do I add my own on/off settings?
faq.a: Pass `toggles` with a `key`, `label` and optional `detail` for each. Their state lives in `value.toggles`, keyed by `key`.

faq.q: Can the spend cap use other amounts or a currency?
faq.a: Yes. `caps` sets the amounts the minus and plus buttons step through, and `formatCap` sets how the amount reads. `capLabel` and `capDetail` change the text beside it.
